objective: Finish every remaining performance finding and verify the full release gate.

findings.title: Move session dialog counts and PDF targets off the UI thread
findings.original_follow_up: Use a debounced, coalesced QueryOp request carrying the profile, collection, filters and one classifier. Reuse classification metadata within that request and load PDF titles/progress in batches. Show a loading state and discard closed, superseded or profile-switched results. Reuse LatestQuery where appropriate.
findings.implementation: Debounced background session counts, one classifier/pool snapshot, batched PDF targets
findings.measurement: 10,000 cards / 20 tag rows: **1,125.1 → 59.5 ms**; 504 → 24 SQL reads; 42 → 1 classifier resolutions

findings.title: Reuse EPUB metadata and a reverse section path map
findings.original_follow_up: Keep a bounded snapshot for the active document, keyed by captured profile, filename, metadata identity and sanitizer version. Build a validated path-to-section map once. Clear it on replacement, sanitization changes, document/profile switch and close. Preserve containment checks; never cache arbitrary path acceptance.
findings.implementation: Active-EPUB metadata snapshot and validated reverse section map
findings.measurement: Cold last-section lookup in a 10 MB / 200-section book: **1,356.5 → 8.2 ms**; 201 → 1 JSON reads. Warm: 0 reads

findings.title: Combine statistics updates within each review event
findings.original_follow_up: Synchronous durable writes remain; do not disable durability to optimize them.
findings.implementation: Combined statistics totals and tag-attribution persistence
findings.measurement: First batch: **97.0 → 55.8 ms** with 512 populated tags; 4 → 2 durable saves per review cycle

findings.title: Stop scanning the PDF library for each reviewer source cover
findings.original_follow_up: Resolve a verified source card identity directly when available. Otherwise use a batched, collection-generation-scoped derived filename index with exact-match precedence and the existing unique-fuzzy fallback. Reuse the resolved payload between the two sides of one card and invalidate after relevant note/document changes.
findings.implementation: Background, generation-scoped PDF source index and question/answer payload reuse
findings.measurement: 20 lookups / 4,000 PDFs: **59.7 → 11.1 ms including index construction**; warm lookups add 0.004 ms; 80,000 per-note loads avoided

findings.title: Address FTS maintenance scans during document replacement
findings.original_follow_up: Fresh insertion overhead is measured in fts_tradeoffs.json; profile real upgrade sizes.
findings.implementation: Stable indexed FTS identities for replacement/deletion
findings.measurement: First batch: 4,000-page replacement **814.0 → 126.5 ms**. Fresh insertion still has the documented 70 ms tradeoff

findings.title: Make knowledge tree validation linear and persist only changed rows
findings.original_follow_up: Define timestamp semantics before implementing changed-row persistence and batched multi-node edits.
findings.implementation: Iterative validation plus structural-change-only tree writes
findings.measurement: First batch deep validation: 275.6 → 11.1 ms. Completion 4,000-node unchanged save: **10.81 → 5.54 ms**, 4,000 → 0 updated rows; leaf move updates 1 row

findings.title: Bound database inspection and avoid quadratic text highlighting
findings.original_follow_up: Move discovery/lookup/formatting into a captured-profile cancellable read operation, with explicit selection, row and byte budgets and paging. Group entries by card once. Precompute UTF-16 offsets once or use a stable Qt-native search strategy, debounce queries and update only the active selection on navigation.
findings.implementation: Cancellable, paged, read-only database inspection; compact Unicode offsets
findings.measurement: 1,000 positions in 312,000 characters: **152.1 → 11.7 ms**. Each inspection page bounds cards, rows, text and elapsed work

findings.title: Keep empty PDF preparation from falling back to UI extraction
findings.original_follow_up: Move webpage rendering, cover generation, managed copying/indexing and Qt-only fallback work off the UI path with lifecycle coverage.
findings.implementation: PDF copy, cover, native fallback and indexing in the collection worker; prepared empty text retained
findings.measurement: 200-page native import: longest sampled UI event-pump gap **63.1 → 13.8 ms**; UI pumps 0 → 14. One sample; not an import-throughput claim

findings.title: Build the bookmark index in one pass
findings.original_follow_up: Folder subtree indexes and deferred DOM mounting require separate rendering measurements.
findings.implementation: One private bookmark accumulator, iterative deep traversal, folder ranges and selection prefix counts
findings.measurement: First batch: 5,000 opaque IDs 2,065 → 3.7 ms. 1,000 counts over 10,000 bookmarks: **373.2 → 0.076 ms warm**; separate range construction 1.03 ms, selection-prefix setup excluded

findings.title: Debounce full writing preview and serialize saves outside typing handlers
findings.original_follow_up: Keep caret/status updates immediate, debounce preview and word-count snapshots, and skip preview parsing while hidden. Capture immutable text/profile/card generations for an ordered background save queue; retain a safe close/profile-switch flush and visible failure handling. Persist unchanged editor state only when dirty.
findings.implementation: Debounced/hidden-aware markdown preview and one ordered background save queue
findings.measurement: Twenty edits of 105,000 characters: markdown parse work **142.1 → 6.9 ms**, 20 → 1 parses; hidden preview: 0 parses

findings.title: Remove repeated global set differences in Undo tracking
findings.original_follow_up: SQL boundary was excluded from the benchmark.
findings.implementation: Local Undo/Redo membership checks instead of repeated global history differences
findings.measurement: First batch Python transition: **310.5 → 3.0 ms** at 4,000 cards. Newly measured real SQLite boundary: 2.74 ms / 12 queries for 10,000 revlog IDs

findings.title: Reduce search candidate amplification and repeated tokenization
findings.original_follow_up: Compile query terms once per request, reduce redundant text work and use incremental candidate batches with cancellation and explicit work/byte budgets. Evaluate proper text indexes for excerpts with the required fallback. Move current-document searches to debounced latest-request workers. Preserve ranking, prefix, phrase and Unicode semantics rather than just lowering caps.
findings.implementation: Compiled queries, streaming candidate batches, bounded top-result ranking, async current-document search
findings.measurement: Same 1,200 ranked results / 12,000 pages: **129.1 → 104.1 ms**; peak Python allocation **7.18 → 0.61 MB**, 91.5% less

findings.title: Make EPUB progress events update only position-dependent state
findings.original_follow_up: Query highlights for the active section using the existing card/section index. Cache section counts and panel data per document generation; invalidate on highlight/source/bookmark mutations. Separate position persistence from section-change and visible-panel updates.
findings.implementation: Section-scoped EPUB highlight reads and position-only progress updates
findings.measurement: 20,000 saved highlights / 100 in current section: **23.75 → 0.103 ms**; 20,000 → 100 materialized rows

findings.title: Avoid materializing every peer in large duplicate groups
findings.original_follow_up: Represent exact-equivalence groups compactly and resolve selected peers lazily. Keep fuzzy edges separate because fuzzy similarity is not transitive; connected components alone cannot replace direct-match semantics. Reuse one computed match model within each shelf snapshot.
findings.implementation: Shared exact-duplicate groups, lazy peer expansion, separate fuzzy edges
findings.measurement: 800 same-origin documents: **61.1 → 13.6 ms**; 639,200 → 1,600 stored references; Python peak 37.6 → 5.87 MB

findings.title: Batch remaining branch and linked-media inspection paths
findings.original_follow_up: Extend operation-owned batch projections to the remaining consumers, limit branch study reads to required structure/metadata, and reuse one classifier and adjacency map. Use deque for breadth-first traversal. Put synchronous read previews in QueryOp and ordinary mutations in CollectionOp. Batch supplemental writes transactionally, preserving per-card errors and native Undo semantics.
findings.implementation: Batched branch/media projections and supplemental writes; background previews and native mutation operations
findings.measurement: Shift 4,000 priorities: **341.8 → 16.0 ms**; 4,000 → 1 commits, 4,000 → 5 priority reads

findings.title: Prevent PDF Find highlighting from observing its own writes
findings.original_follow_up: Observe text-layer lifecycle once, or disconnect/suppress the observer around owned writes and reconnect afterward. Make highlighting idempotent and modify only changed spans. Do not mutate PDF.js selection structure gratuitously.
findings.implementation: Disconnect the Find observer around owned writes; idempotent marks; preserve PDF.js text changes
findings.measurement: 1,000 spans plus one external update over 10 frames: **10 → 2 render callbacks**, **89.1 → 5.2 ms** highlight work; one headless-browser sample

findings.title: Add cancellation and resource budgets inside PDF extraction
findings.original_follow_up: Introduce cooperative checks between pages, a bounded extraction result/stream strategy, and explicit subprocess time/output budgets with termination cleanup. Consider a dedicated process for non-cooperative native work, using the existing annotation-process lifecycle as a reference, without assuming arbitrary thread parallelism is safe.
findings.implementation: Per-page cancellation plus time/page/output budgets and bounded/reaped external extractor
findings.measurement: Cancel after page 2 of 1,000: **48.4 → 2.93 ms** return time; 1,000 → 2 loaded pages, documents closed in both cases

findings.title: Bound Qt and React item creation after background reads
findings.original_follow_up: Measure callback/commit time separately from query time. Use a model/view or paged/windowed representation for large collections, or bounded generation-aware construction batches. Preserve selection, expanded state, stable row order, accessibility and immediate cancellation of obsolete builds.
findings.implementation: Bounded Qt construction, deferred bookmark folders, 100-row imports and 50-row PDF highlights
findings.measurement: React SSR: closed 10,000-leaf folder **92.6 → 0.246 ms**; import rows **413.1 → 4.89 ms**. Qt 5,000 rows: 1 → 126 callbacks; see timing caveat below

findings.title: Load bookshelf thumbnails for visible tiles with a byte budget
findings.original_follow_up: Prioritize viewport tiles with a small prefetch margin and an LRU byte budget; debounce filtering and reuse stable items where practical. Keep bounded parallel decoding only after measuring file/CPU pressure, and mark collection-free image work explicitly where supported.
findings.implementation: Visible/prefetched thumbnails, debounced filters and 24 MiB derived-image LRU
findings.measurement: Initial viewport / 2,000 covers: **918.0 → 4.11 ms** native decode work; 2,000 → 9 images; raster accounting 409.6 → 1.84 MB

findings.title: Split extension runtime chunks by actual consumers
findings.original_follow_up: Separate non-React bridge/browser/i18n core from UI hooks and settings/export validation. Investigate loading custom-pack validation only when needed while preserving validation before use. Remove forced all-shared cohabitation and inspect static entry graphs after a reproducible build.
findings.implementation: Split non-React core, UI and lazy custom-language validation chunks
findings.measurement: Static content-script graph **1,001,053 → 192,642 bytes**, 80.8% smaller; background 986,486 → 177,928; offscreen 950,623 → 142,059

findings.title: Share media detection across heartbeat paths
findings.original_follow_up: Capture media context once per tick/event and pass it to both protocol payload builders. Track the active video via bounded lifecycle discovery, prefer a linear maximum selection over sorting, and reduce idle polling while retaining navigation/reinjection detection. Flush final progress on hide/pagehide before suspending.
findings.implementation: One media sample for both heartbeat protocols, live video collection and hidden-poll suspension
findings.measurement: 1,000 visible ticks: **2.86 → 2.24 ms**, 2,000 → 0 warm DOM queries; same 2,000 protocol messages. Hidden periodic ticks emit 0; playback events still flush

findings.title: Index SuperMemo parents once and batch supplemental schedule writes
findings.original_follow_up: Build an element-ID lookup once and reuse it for parent metadata. Batch topic-state rows in the existing controlled supplemental transaction boundary where failure recovery allows. Keep ImportOperation journal/bind/commit durability boundaries intact; do not bulk-disable journaling to improve a benchmark.
findings.implementation: One SuperMemo parent map and one batch of supplemental topic schedules
findings.measurement: 256-topic native import: **119.7 → 97.6 ms**; 36,992 → 4,352 element-ID reads; 256 → 1 topic commits; journal durability retained

findings.title: Profile eager imports and first database use before changing startup
findings.original_follow_up: Capture cold/warm import self/cumulative time, profile-open stages and first-DB-use time in a disposable synthetic environment. Lazy-load optional dialogs only when the measurement supports it; register hooks idempotently and initialize language before visible strings. Separate safe connection fast paths from potentially waiting initialization without sharing connections across threads.
findings.implementation: Defer six optional dialog modules; initialize SQLite outside the registry lock
findings.measurement: **21.7 ms** isolated optional import group deferred to first use. Under a controlled 100 ms initializer stall, unrelated cached lookup **110.1 → 0.002 ms**; first schema open 6.98 → 6.69 ms

findings.title: Reuse normalized config within each reviewer event
findings.original_follow_up: Resolve one event-local normalized snapshot and classifier, passing them through configured helpers. Consider a versioned read cache only inside config_service with explicit invalidation for every save and supported external edits. Do not maintain independent consumer caches that can disagree with Settings.
findings.implementation: One normalized config/classifier snapshot per reviewer event
findings.measurement: 100 events with 20 populated presets: **261.9 → 96.1 ms**, 300 → 100 config reads

current_work: All 24 findings implemented, benchmarked and verified by the complete release gate.
